targetAudience.primary: Engineers designing agent runtimes, credential brokers and layered configuration systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands configuration precedence, environment-based providers and trust boundaries.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A lower-trust project layer can remain able to steer broker-owned inputs even when a higher layer nominally wins precedence.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change removes protected provider and shell-startup inputs from project configuration only when credential brokering is effectively enabled.

externalHook.description: Winning a merge is weaker than owning the right to participate in a sensitive decision.

coreProposition: Security-sensitive layered configuration must model authority ownership separately from value precedence: when an effective policy gives a credential broker control of provider and startup inputs, lower-trust project configuration should lose that decision surface rather than merely lose a value comparison.

originalValue.description: Reframes broker hardening as an ownership transfer that activates with effective broker state, while exposing classifier drift and higher-layer scope as separate obligations.

readerTakeaway: Record who owns each sensitive configuration decision, remove owned inputs from unauthorized layers when that owner is active, and audit suppressed keys without logging their values.

supported: The merged change distinguishes unconfigured, disabled and enabled broker states.
The enabled branch removes project shell snapshot/profile controls and protected provider/startup environment keys.
The disabled branch preserves ordinary project shell configuration.
unsupported: Isolation from every user, host, managed-policy or process source
uncertain: How protected-key classification evolves with new providers
Which higher configuration layers intentionally retain authority

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article establishes a general configuration-governance pattern without a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged mechanism and branch-specific tests support a precise distinction between configuration authority and precedence with explicit limits.
